number.why: The source supports 13/81 versus 13/71 for postoperative AF lasting at least 5 minutes during hospitalization. These counts yield the served reconstructed RR of 0.8765432098765431. The published 0.85 and 95% CI 0.37–1.99 describe an OR, not the reconstructed RR. The denominators include all randomized patients, supporting the numerical analysis population, although the source does not explicitly label the analysis intention-to-treat.

quotes.span: The remaining 152 patients were randomized to receive colchicine (n = 81) or placebo (n = 71) ( ).
The primary efficacy endpoint was the development of at least one episode of AF (lasting 5 minutes or longer) occurring after cardiac surgery at any point during hospitalization.

The rate of AF was 16.0% (n = 13) in the colchicine group, versus 18.3% (n = 13) in the placebo group. Comparing the colchicine and placebo groups, the odds ratio was 0.85 (95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.37–1.99).
Among the 152 randomized patients, AF occurred in 26 patients (17%), including 16% of patients in the colchicine group and 18.3% of patients in the placebo group.

Six patients died during hospitalization because of surgical complications, including four patients in the placebo group and two patients in the colchicine group. All six patients were included in the analysis.

entry.why: The trial enrolled adults undergoing elective cardiac surgery and compared peri-operative colchicine with placebo. This establishes entry within the question's population. Eligibility restricted enrollment to patients in sinus rhythm without previous AF; it does not establish applicability to every cardiac-surgery population.

quotes.span: Inclusion Criteria: * All patients aged 18 years or above undergoing elective cardiac surgery. * Sinus rhythm and no previous AF * Agreed to sign informed consent.

Upon enrollment, patients were treated with 1 mg of colchicine or matching placebo 12 to 24 hours prior to surgery, followed by colchicine (0.5 mg) or placebo immediately after their surgery (via a nasogastric tube) and daily treatment at this dose until hospital discharge.

missed: No additional finding changes either verdict. The inclusion of deaths in the analysis strengthens the denominator interpretation, but an explicit intention-to-treat designation remains unestablished. The trial should be named END-AF Low Dose rather than described ambiguously as COPPS-type: evidence/held/32720823/PMC7388125.xml states, "The present study, END-AF Low Dose, is an investigator-initiated trial that evaluated the effect of low-dose colchicine (1 mg administered 12–24 hours prior to cardiac surgery, followed by 0.5 mg daily until discharge) on the incidence of POAF and adverse events, particularly colchicine-related gastrointestinal (GI) side effects."
